issues.where: The pattern across all four is the same
issues.explanation: Mildly editorial framing for a BLUF that otherwise stays factual. The 'same pattern' framing leans on the cross-cutting theme; a branch chief reading BLUF in 90 seconds should be able to evaluate the claim quickly.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider replacing with: 'Three of the four describe the same pattern: units and SOF moving faster than TDDG's institutional cycle.' Direct, no editorial.

issues.explanation: One of the four cited articles is dated February 2026, not May 2026. The article previews the May Ivy Mass red-team event but the source itself predates the bulletin month. Acceptable because the May event is the subject, but the date is honest and visible.
issues.suggested_fix: If a Defense One follow-up on Ivy Mass appears in late May or early June, swap the citation. Until then, leave it with the date as published - do not paper over the publication date.

issues.where: Single item from a single article
issues.explanation: Branch 4 (Learning Science) has only one item sourced from one article. The section is honest but thin. A branch chief might reasonably ask why this isn't combined into the cross-cutting theme.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the Branch 4 section as is; the implication is specific enough (measurable competencies, BCT pilot, validation guard-rails) to justify standing alone. Note the thinness in the BLUF if it persists next month.

issues.where: Single theme supported by exactly 3 articles
issues.explanation: The cross-cutting theme meets the >=3-article minimum exactly. The framing is defensible but a more conservative bulletin might require >=4 articles for a theme when the corpus is small (4 articles total).
issues.suggested_fix: Acceptable for this month given source diversity. If the focused-source pilot continues at 4-5 articles per month, consider raising the theme threshold to >=4 in monthly_synthesis.md.

issues.where: the most actionable PME prescription published this month
issues.explanation: Mildly superlative framing. 'Most actionable' is a judgement call without explicit comparison.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace 'most actionable' with 'a concrete' - the article speaks for itself without the superlative.
